title: Canonical global-germ and constant arrows for Kummer line families
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $m>0$ with $mA=0$, and $L_T=\mu_{m,T}\otimes A$ the existing finite etale Tate line [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. For a field $k$, a $k$-scheme $p:B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and either curve $C$ of [def-pur-kummer-line-geometry], define $C_B=C\times_kB$ and $a_B$ by the actual pullback [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $G(T)=R\Gamma(T,L_T)$ and $I(f)=Rf_*L_X$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. For every geometric point $s$ of $B$, define the natural global-germ map from sections to the stalk by the terminal etale object and its germ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Its derived map, preceded by the inverse canonical Leray comparison, defines $G(X)\to I(f)_s$. For a primitive $m$-th root $\zeta\in k$, define $c_T:A_T\to L_T$ by $a\mapsto\zeta\otimes a$, and its transpose $A[0]\to G(T)$ under the constant-sheaf/sections derived adjunction. Define the untwisted unit as $A_B[0]\xrightarrow{c_B}L_B\to I(f)$ using the normalized finite-twist unit of [def-pur-relative-kummer-canonical-arrows], and define its germ using the canonical constant-stalk identification. These constructions use the module-valued strict-local restriction interface [def-pur-module-strict-local-restriction] and the constant sheaf of [def-pur-kummer-exchange-class-arrows].
